gen-archivo-black-gf-quando: Archivo Black sounds authoritative and urban, its lowercase filling the middle of the line with plenty of space around each letter. It declares; Quando, a bookish serif, lingers with wide, sparse spacing.
gen-audiowide-fs-gambetta: Gambetta reads graceful and bookish, its stroke weight shifting noticeably but never dramatically. Audiowide does its best work as an uninterrupted monoline, futuristic and tech-minded, while Gambetta handles the shading.
gen-audiowide-gf-abyssinica-sil: Tiled, fixed-width futurism on top, soft watercolor shading below. What stands out most: Audiowide keeps one fixed stroke thickness, while Abyssinica SIL carries robust downstrokes with slender turns.
gen-audiowide-gf-cambo: Futuristic and tile-like on top, refined and bookish beneath. Audiowide holds its thickness steady around every curve, and Cambo adds a mild, approachable stroke contrast with a short step from lowercase to capital height.
gen-audiowide-gf-fanwood-text: Literary and bookish, this serif has a large-eyed lowercase and gently swelling curves. Fanwood Text gives a modest stem-to-hairline ratio to sit under Audiowide, whose strokes look laser-cut at a single width.
gen-audiowide-gf-holtwood-one-sc: Futuristic up top, authoritative below, and nothing about it whispers. Audiowide runs a single track width like a neon sign tube, while Holtwood One SC spreads wide-tracked, its curves closing up to slivers.
gen-audiowide-gf-manuale: Futuristic letters that look traced with a marker, set like tiles with wide gaps. And Manuale, traditional and editorial, runs on a large-eyed lowercase and soft fat-to-slim strokes that keep paragraphs flowing.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-naskh-arabic: Audiowide is futuristic, one flat line weight running through every glyph. The gap is what stands out: Noto Naskh Arabic is a refined serif with a mild taper like lightly engraved brass and a very tall x-height.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-nastaliq-urdu: Noto Nastaliq Urdu feels editorial and dignified, with tight vertical rhythm and joins that slim noticeably. But Audiowide, stencil-cut at one steady width and unmistakably futuristic, makes it feel quieter and more formal beside it.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-rashi-hebrew: Strokes that never swell or thin, fixed from stem to curve, give Audiowide its tech-tile look. It earns its keep big and short; Noto Rashi Hebrew stays bookish.
